body:
Blackstone closed its fifth energy transition private equity fund at $8.7 billion, exceeding its predecessor by over 50 percent and reaching its hard cap within a year of launch.

According to ESG Today, Blackstone Energy Transition Partners (BETP) targets control-oriented equity investments across the energy transition value chain, including equipment, service and technology providers, as well as large-scale infrastructure projects aimed at decarbonization. The fund excludes investments in hydrocarbon reserves and extraction.

The global investment giant has positioned itself to capture what it views as significant opportunities in energy transition and climate-related infrastructure. In 2022, Blackstone indicated it expects to deploy an estimated $100 billion in energy transition and climate change solutions over the next decade.

BETP V was launched in late 2025, following the final close of the fund’s fourth vintage earlier that year at $5.6 billion. The latest fundraising success represents a more than 50 percent increase over the prior vintage.

David Foley, Global Head of Blackstone Energy Transition Partners, stated that the firm sees a generational opportunity for experienced investors to provide solutions to challenges posed by growing electricity demand.

Deployment Underway Across Multiple Platforms

The fund began its investment period in June and has already funded three platform companies, as ESG Today reports. These include Kindle, a North America power generation platform; Fisterra, an energy transition and sustainability asset developer and investment company; and Viridon, an electric transmission platform.

BETP V has also completed three acquisitions: Flow Control Systems, a data center cooling solutions provider; Dresser Utility Solutions, a utilities-focused measurement, control and repair company; and DarkVision, which provides energy infrastructure asset inspection services.

Blackstone reports that BETP’s energy transition investments have generated a 34 percent net internal rate of return since 1997, underscoring the firm’s long-standing presence in the sector and its ability to generate returns in an evolving energy landscape.

With information from ESG Today
